title: Level 1 (Beginner) - B-18
notes:
West leads the ♥10 against 6NT. After winning the opening heart lead, South is faced with playing the club suit for 1 loser. As the ♣A must always be lost, South cannot afford to lose a trick to the ♣Q.

If South leads a low club out of his hand and West follows with the ♣6, South must decide whether to play dummy's ♣K or a low club. Playing the ♣K from dummy will work for only one distribution of the defenders' clubs, when East has a singleton ♣Q.

Playing a club other than the ♣K from dummy is a superior play because it works in two cases. This play will succeed when East has the singleton ♣A and when West has all 3 clubs. In the latter case, East will discard. South can cross back to his hand and again lead clubs through West.
